title: Graph isomorphism: moderately exponential vs quasi-polynomial
problem_statement: Given two graphs on n vertices, decide whether they are isomorphic.

algorithms.name: brute force over permutations
algorithms.pseudocode: for each permutation pi: if pi maps E1 onto E2: yes

algorithms.name: Babai-Luks canonical labeling
algorithms.idea: Group-theoretic divide-and-conquer combined with Zemlyachenko's degree-reduction trick.

algorithms.name: Babai's quasi-polynomial algorithm
algorithms.idea: Luks's group-theoretic framework plus new combinatorial partitioning (local certificates, Split-or-Johnson).
algorithms.correctness: Babai 2016; see caveats for the 2017 correction.

relationship: n! -> exp(sqrt(n log n)) -> quasi-polynomial exp(polylog n). A polynomial-time algorithm is open. Polynomial algorithms exist for restricted classes, e.g. bounded degree (Luks 1982).

sources.title: Isomorphism of graphs of bounded valence can be tested in polynomial time
sources.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 25(1), 42-65

caveats: In January 2017 Harald Helfgott found an error in the analysis of Babai's algorithm. Babai repaired it within days, restoring the quasi-polynomial bound. GI is not known to be NP-complete (that would collapse the polynomial hierarchy to its second level). No efficient quantum algorithm is known either: the relevant hidden subgroup problem over the symmetric group resists Fourier sampling.
notes: Interesting for the quantum question because quantum computers are NOT known to help here, unlike factoring.
